memos.scout:
The honest case for buying VWA now is weak, and I don't think the brief supports one.

What the brief does show: the coin is alive, up about 106x over 30 minutes, with 44 buyers and 9.85 SOL bought in the last 15 minutes, and the drawdown from its 30-minute high is only 0.2%. Pool depth is about 879 SOL, so a $20 ticket would have modest impact.

But the demand looks manufactured. The curve data shows one bundle taking 100% of buyers and the top 3 holding everything. The first two minutes after graduation saw 780 SOL bought, almost all from a launch bot, with a sell-to-buy ratio of zero. That is an operator-backed launch. Recent volume has real sellers now (8.2 SOL sold against 9.85 bought, 29 sellers), so the operator-controlled supply is starting to exit into whatever retail demand remains. The flat 0.2% drawdown is what a stalled pool looks like before a dump, not evidence of durable support.

Against that, the base rate for operator-backed coins is roughly break-even before fees, and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost makes a 30-60 minute hold negative in expectation unless the coin keeps rising. Nothing here says it will.

Verdict: skip. There is no credible case that real demand will
